extraFacts.fact: A recovery winch is a vehicle-mounted winch for pulling and recovering vehicles, and an industrial winch is a work winch for lifting and pulling in fixed and plant duty; the pounds figure in the model name is the rated line pull.
extraFacts.source: Pierce winch model naming as shown in the Indus size table (e.g. PS6000 = 6,000 lb. Recovery Winch)

faqs.q: What are Pierce electric and hydraulic winches, cables and parts used for?
faqs.a: The Pierce range covers 25 listed items: electric recovery and industrial winches, hydraulic recovery and industrial winches, winch cables with standard or swivel hooks, a 12 V motor and a 12 V solenoid. Pick a winch on its line pull, drum and drive (12 V electric, AC or hydraulic), then the cable and parts from the same table.

faqs.q: How do I read Pierce winch part numbers such as PS6000, PS654-11EK and PSHV15000?
faqs.a: In the table PS6000, PS9000, PS12000 and PS20000 are recovery winches named for their pull in pounds, while PS654 numbers are industrial winches with the drum size in the number (PS654-8EK has an 8 inch drum, PS654-11EK an 11 inch drum). Hydraulic winches start PSH, as in PSHV15000 (15,000 lb) and PSHDH20000 (20,000 lb).

faqs.q: What line pull ratings do the Pierce recovery winches have?
faqs.a: The Pierce recovery winches in this listing are rated 6,000 lb (PS6000), 9,000 lb (PS9000), 12,000 lb (PS12000) and 20,000 lb (PS20000) for the electric versions, and 18,000 lb (PSHV18000) and 20,000 lb (PSHDH20000) for the hydraulic ones. The rating is the figure in the item name, so choose one with margin over the heaviest pull.

faqs.q: Which Pierce industrial winches are electric and which are hydraulic?
faqs.a: The Pierce industrial winches come as AC electric, 12 V electric and hydraulic models. The AC ones are PS654-11EK at 7,500 lb and PS654-11EMK at 11,000 lb on an 11 inch drum, plus PS654-8EK and PS654-8EMK on an 8 inch drum; the 12 V ones are PSW654-11K at 9,000 lb and PSW654-11MK at 12,500 lb; the hydraulic ones are PSHV10000 at 10,000 lb and PSHV15000 at 15,000 lb.

faqs.q: What Pierce winch cable sizes and hook types are listed?
faqs.a: The Pierce winch cables in this listing are 3/8 inch and 1/2 inch, with a standard or swivel hook. PS0362 is a 3/8 inch cable with a standard hook and PS0362SS a 3/8 inch cable with a swivel hook, and PS0383SS is a 1/2 inch by 100 ft cable with a swivel hook. Match the diameter to the drum and the winch rating.

faqs.q: Are the Pierce PSW654 winches 12 volt, and what does a 12 V winch need?
faqs.a: Yes, PSW654-11K and PSW654-11MK are listed as 12 volt industrial winches with an 11 inch drum, rated 9,000 lb and 12,500 lb. A 12 V winch needs a supply that can carry the motor current, so check your vehicle or battery and the matching winch motor (PS534H) and solenoid (P0375) before you order.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a standard hook and a swivel hook on a Pierce winch cable?
faqs.a: A swivel hook turns on the cable end so the load can rotate without twisting the cable, while a standard hook is fixed. The listing has both on its 3/8 inch cables, for example PS0362 (standard) and PS0362SS (swivel), so choose the swivel where the load can spin.

faqs.q: Which Pierce winch parts are listed besides winches and cables?
faqs.a: Besides the winches and cables the listing includes the PS534H 12 V winch motor and the P0375 12 V winch solenoid. Remotes are listed separately; see the [Pierce winch remote controls](/p/pierce-winch-remote-controls) for the corded and wireless options.

faqs.q: How should a Pierce hydraulic winch be installed on a hydraulic circuit?
faqs.a: A hydraulic winch such as the PSHV15000 runs from a hydraulic supply, so match the pump flow and pressure to the winch before you plumb it. Check the hose and fittings are rated at least as high as the circuit, and test the brake and the line pull with a light load first.

faqs.q: Which Pierce winch suits a 12,000 lb recovery duty?
faqs.a: For a 12,000 lb recovery the table lists PS12000, a 12,000 lb recovery winch, and the hydraulic 18,000 lb PSHV18000 and 20,000 lb PSHDH20000 for heavier jobs. Allow margin over the heaviest pull and check the cable size and hook rating suit the winch you choose.

faqs.q: How do the Pierce electric and hydraulic industrial winches compare?
faqs.a: The electric industrial winches in this listing run on AC (PS654 models) or 12 V (PSW654-11K and -11MK), while the hydraulic ones (PSHV10000, PSHV15000, PSW654-11HK, PSW654-8HK) run from a hydraulic supply. Use electric where a power supply is at hand and hydraulic where the machine already has a hydraulic circuit.

faqs.q: What are Pierce winch remote controls used for?
faqs.a: The Pierce winch remote controls let an operator run a winch without standing at it. The listing has four part numbers: CP077K, a 2 button remote for power up/power down pumps; CP079K, a 6 button remote with a 15 foot cord; CP271, a 2 button winch remote with a vulcanized plug; and PS002, a wireless remote system.

faqs.q: How do I choose between the Pierce remote part numbers CP077K, CP079K, CP271 and PS002?
faqs.a: The item text tells them apart: CP077K and CP271 are 2 button remotes, CP079K is a 6 button corded remote with a 15 foot cord, and PS002 is the wireless remote system. Remotes are listed against the winches they fit, so quote the winch part number with the remote you need.

faqs.q: What is the Pierce CP079K 6 button remote with a 15 foot cord?
faqs.a: The CP079K is a 6 button winch remote with a 15 foot cord, the corded option with the most controls in this listing. It suits a winch where the operator can stay on the cord, while the 2 button remotes cover simple in and out control.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Pierce CP077K and CP271 2 button remotes?
faqs.a: Both are 2 button remotes, but CP077K is listed for power up/power down pumps and CP271 as a winch remote with a vulcanized plug. Match the remote to the plug and control the winch or pump has, and quote the winch part number so we confirm the fit.

faqs.q: What does the Pierce PS002 wireless remote system include?
faqs.a: The listing names PS002 only as a wireless remote system and gives no further detail. Ask us for the contents, range and the winches it works with before you order, and quote the winch part number.

faqs.q: What voltage and rating are the Pierce winch remote controls?
faqs.a: The listing gives no voltage or rating for the Pierce winch remotes, only that they are listed against the winches they fit. Ask us to confirm the voltage and current for your winch before you order a remote.

faqs.q: What kind of plug does the Pierce CP271 winch remote have?
faqs.a: The CP271 has a vulcanized plug, listed as a 2 button winch remote. Check that the plug matches the socket on your winch before ordering.

faqs.q: Is there a datasheet or wiring diagram for the Pierce winch remotes?
faqs.a: The listing carries no datasheet or wiring diagram for the remotes. Send us the part number and your winch part number, and we request the maker's wiring and fitting information before you order.

faqs.q: Which Pierce winches do the remote controls fit?
faqs.a: The Pierce remotes are listed against the winches they fit, and the listing does not publish the pairing. Quote the winch from the [Pierce electric and hydraulic winches table](/p/pierce-electric-and-hydraulic-winches-cables-and-parts), and we confirm which remote suits it.

faqs.q: How should a Pierce winch remote be installed and tested?
faqs.a: Connect the remote to the winch control with the power off, then test in and out with no load before you rely on it. Keep the cord clear of the drum and cable, and replace a damaged cord rather than repairing it.

faqs.q: How do the Pierce corded and wireless winch remotes compare?
faqs.a: The corded remotes (CP077K, CP079K and CP271) are limited by their cord, with the CP079K reaching 15 feet, while the PS002 wireless system has no cord. Choose wireless where the operator needs to move away from the winch, and corded where a cable is simpler.
